claim: After a written rent demand, the tenant has 3 days, not counting Saturdays, Sundays and court-observed holidays, before the landlord may end the lease for unpaid rent.
quote: If the tenant fails to pay rent when due and the default continues for 3 days, excluding Saturday, Sunday, and legal holidays, after delivery of written demand by the landlord for payment of the rent or possession of the premises, the landlord may terminate the rental agreement. Legal holidays for the purpose of this section shall be court-observed holidays only.

claim: Lease-ending notices must be mailed, hand-delivered, e-mailed under s. 83.505, or left at the home if the tenant is away, and a lease cannot waive these notice rules.
value: Lease-ending notices must be mailed, hand-delivered, e-mailed under s. 83.505, or left at the home if the tenant is away, and a lease cannot waive these notice rules.
quote: The delivery of the written notices required by subsections (1)-(3) shall be by mailing, delivering a true copy thereof, e-mailing in accordance with s. 83.505, or, if the tenant is absent from the premises, by leaving a copy thereof at the residence. The notice requirements of subsections (1)-(3) may not be waived in the rental agreement.

claim: In an eviction case, a tenant raising any defense other than payment must pay the alleged rent into the court registry, or file a motion to determine rent, within 5 days (not counting weekends and legal holidays) of being served, or lose those defenses and face an immediate default judgment.
quote: to determine the amount of rent to be paid into the registry within 5 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, after the date of service of process constitutes an absolute waiver of the tenant’s defenses other than payment, and the landlord is entitled to an immediate default judgment for removal of the tenant with a writ of possession to issue without further notice or hearing thereon.

claim: Florida LIHEAP (state program) requires that at least one person in the household is a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or qualified alien.
value: At least one person in your household is a U.S. Citizen, permanent resident or qualified alien of the U.S.
quote: At least one person in your household is a U.S. Citizen, permanent resident or qualified alien of the U.S.
notes: The Miami-Dade page (us-fl-miamidade.liheap.status-requirement) words this as the applicant being a citizen or LPR. The state FAQ says one household member suffices. Proration of the benefit for mixed households was not found on the state FAQ; not verified here.
